title: Indian Restaurants Sweep UK's Nation's Curry Awards 2026
excerpt: Aarti in Leeds took the overall Curry Restaurant of the Year title and Kolshi Premier in Warwick won Indian Restaurant of the Year at the 4th Nation's Curry Awards, celebrating the UK's vibrant curry industry.
body:
• Aarti in Leeds won overall Curry Restaurant of the Year at the 4th Nation's Curry Awards 2026
  • Kolshi Premier Indian Restaurant in Warwick was named overall Indian Restaurant of the Year
  • The ceremony celebrated winners across regions including Scotland, Wales, North, Midlands, and South England
  • The UK's curry industry is valued at £4 billion and remains a vital part of the country's cultural identity
  • Regional winners included Firangi in Cambuslang (Scotland), Bangor Tandoori (Wales), and The Coriander Club in Reading (South)

Leeds and Warwick Restaurants Crowned Champions

Indian restaurants across the United Kingdom were recognised at the 4th Nation's Curry Awards 2026, with Aarti in Leeds taking the overall Curry Restaurant of the Year title and Kolshi Premier Indian Restaurant in Warwick winning Indian Restaurant of the Year.

The ceremony, organised by Oceanic Awards and held in Huddersfield on February 9, celebrated excellence across the UK's curry industry, drawing finalists from every region of the country, according to the Bury Times and the South Wales Chronicle.

Regional Winners Across the UK

The awards spanned multiple categories and regions, reflecting the geographic reach of South Asian cuisine in Britain. In the Curry Restaurant of the Year category, regional winners included Gandhi Indian Restaurant in Stoke on Trent (Midlands), The Coriander Club in Reading (South), Bangor Tandoori Restaurant in Wales, and Firangi in Cambuslang, Scotland.

Firangi, located in a suburb of Glasgow, celebrated its win on social media. "We are officially a Scottish Curry Restaurant of the Year 2026," the restaurant said, according to the Glasgow Times. "This incredible achievement is a testament to our amazing customers who support us every single day, our passionate chefs and dedicated team."

In the Indian Restaurant of the Year category, Bollywood Cottage in Skipton won the North, Elai in Basingstoke took the South, Caernarfon Tandoori won in Wales, and Bombay Lounge in Dalkeith was named Scotland's best.

"We're proud to once again celebrate the finest in the UK's curry scene, recognising the creativity, innovation, and exceptional service that have become synonymous with this beloved cuisine."

— Yasmin Mahmood, CEO of Oceanic Awards

A £4 Billion Industry

The awards arrive amid growing recognition of the curry industry's economic significance. Rushanara Ali, speaking at a related Asian Curry Awards ceremony at the Palace of Westminster earlier this year, underscored the sector's contribution. "This industry is worth £4 billion to the economy, the benefits are huge, both economically and culturally," she said, according to 365Bristol.

The Nation's Curry Awards also recognised standout takeaways and specialty restaurants. Kingsthorpe Spice in Northampton won overall Takeaway of the Year, while Chutney Express in Birmingham was named Outstanding Takeaway of the Year. Lalbagh Indian Restaurant in Cambridge earned the Outstanding Restaurant of the Year title.

Diaspora Connections Run Deep

For the Indian and South Asian diaspora in Britain, the curry industry represents far more than cuisine. Many of the winning establishments are family-run operations built on generational recipes and cultural traditions brought from the subcontinent. Masala Craft in York, which won Bar Curry Restaurant of the Year, is led by owner and chef Arving Mamgain, who relocated his restaurant after rising costs forced a closure in 2022 before reopening at a new location in 2023, according to the Gazette & Herald.

Ahaar Indian Street Food in Prestwich was recognised for excellence in the Street Food category. "At Ahaar, we cook every dish fresh, using traditional methods and real ingredients — no shortcuts, no artificial colours," Head Chef Prasanta Patra said, according to the Bury Times.

Looking Ahead

The 15th English Curry Awards 2026 finalists have already been announced, with winners expected later this year. The Southern Curry Awards, held for the first time in May 2026, saw Dhaba @ 15 in Norwich win overall Curry Restaurant of the Year and Downham Tandoori win Indian Restaurant of the Year, further expanding the network of recognised South Asian restaurants across Britain.
